reasons: Cited Section 13.6.1 selects Delaware law, which is expressly an accepted fallback jurisdiction under GOVLAW, so classifying the clause as compliant (at fallback) and not redlining it is correct per the playbook's classification semantics.

No redline or counterparty comment was produced, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the rendered text is byte-identical to the originals and the deterministic 'governing law within the accepted set' check passes.

The rationale accurately reflects the quoted paragraphs: escalation to Senior Officers, arbitration under Schedule 13.7.3, the IP validity/enforceability/patentability carve-out to a court of competent jurisdiction (13.7.2), and the redacted arbitration procedures/seat. Flagging the unknown seat as a diligence item rather than asserting a walk-away is appropriate, since nothing in the cited text establishes a foreign seat or foreign exclusive venue.
The two shortfalls from preferred wording (no affirmative exclusive-jurisdiction sentence; New York not selected) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than raised as deviations.
